summary: Streaming vs non-streaming token aggregation mismatch reflected on March invoice
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports a 22% discrepancy between token usage shown in the Console (per-request non-streaming totals) and charges on the March invoice, specifically traced to streaming requests. Impact: NovusDocs observed an unexpected $4,300 charge spike on invoice INV-2026-03-74; they are requesting correction or explanation. Customer report received via support form; customer is on Dedicated plan with reserved capacity in us-east.

Observed behavior:
- Non-streaming (batch) requests show 1,120,412 tokens for billing window 2026-03-01 to 2026-03-07 in Console analytics.
- Streaming sessions for same period show per-session deltas that, when summed, equal ~1,372,920 tokens. The invoice token-metered line shows 1,534,230 tokens billed.

Immediate customer ask: reconcile Console totals vs invoice and, if overbilled, issue a credit and explain root cause and mitigation steps.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use customer's API key (sanitized) to replay example streaming session: curl wss://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream with sample payload (see customer transcript).
2) Run identical non-streaming request: POST /v1/generate with same prompt + max_tokens, compare Console per-request token counts under Usage > Requests for the same timestamps.

3) Aggregate streaming session 'token_delta' events from metering-service for timeframe 2026-03-01T00:00:00Z to 2026-03-07T23:59:59Z using query: SELECT sum(token_delta) FROM streaming_events WHERE org_id='novusdocs'
4) Compare results with billing-aggregator: SELECT token_count FROM billing_runs WHERE invoice_id='INV-2026-03-74'
logs: 2026-03-03T14:02:11Z METRICS streaming-proxy req_id=st-0a1b2c conn_id=77 token_delta=184 session_id=sess-92
2026-03-05T03:22:57Z API request_id=nt-9f8e7a model=redwood-llama-13b prompt_tokens=42 completion_tokens=320 total_tokens=362 org=novusdocs
comments: 2026-03-10T09:18 Priya Nair: Customer submitted billing dispute via portal; attaching exported usage CSV and sample streaming transcript. Customer says they do not re-send prompts and never intentionally reconnect mid-stream.
2026-03-10T11:45 Ethan Cole: Assigned - will pull metering pipeline aggregates and compare streaming_event vs billing-aggregator joins. Prioritize due to Dedicated customer and invoice amount.

2026-03-11T16:20 Maya Ruiz (SRE): Observed multiple short-lived streaming connections from NovusDocs between 2026-03-02T12:00 and 12:05 that show reconnects with overlapping 'prefix' tokens; possible duplicate counting if KV cache rehydration duplicated event emission. Opening tracing for streaming-proxy.
investigation_notes:
Initial hypothesis: duplicate token events emitted when streaming client reconnects and streaming-proxy resends recent chunks; metering-service's de-duplication key currently uses (session_id, event_seq) but some reconnect flows create new session_id while re-emitting overlapping deltas.

What we've checked: billing-aggregator reads aggregated token events from billing-topic (Kafka) and does a blind sum. Metering-service has two contributors: 'streaming_events' and 'request_events'. Cross-check shows ~60k tokens present only in billing-topic, not present in Console per-request API (indicating cross-pipeline duplication).

Temporary mitigation: Engineering can subtract duplicated token bucket for this invoice if confirmed; long-term fix options: add streaming-reconnect-id to dedupe key or ensure streaming-proxy tags re-emitted events with 'replay=true' and exclude those in billing-aggregator. See internal runbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/BILL/Streaming+Metering+Runbook
resolution: Pending - awaiting confirmation of dedupe approach and sign-off for retroactive credit. Draft credit calculation prepared (estimate $4,300). Next action: SRE to produce a clean deduped tally by 2026-03-13 and Finance to approve adjustment.
